articles.title: Singapore to join international agreement on neutrality of the Panama Canal - The Straits Times
articles.summary: Singapore to join international agreement on neutrality of the Panama Canal  The Straits TimesPanama President Mulino on 3-day state visit to Singapore  AsiaOnePanamanian President’s trip to Việt Nam marks historic milestone in bilateral relations: ambassador  vietnamnews.vnPanamanian President and spouse begin official visit to Vietnam  Thông tấn xã Việt Nam (TTXVN)Panamanian President embarks on four-day official visit to Viet Nam  en.baochinhp...
articles.full_text:
SINGAPORE – Singapore will join an international agreement to observe and respect the permanent neutrality of the Panama Canal, one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world.
It will also negotiate a bilateral mutual legal assistance agreement with Panama to better tackle transborder crime, said President Tharman Shanmugaratnam on Oct 5 as Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino wrapped up a three-day state visit to Singapore.
President Mulino was in Singapore from Oct 3 to Oct 5 for his first visit to the country as head of state at the invitation of President Tharman. It is the first visit by a Panamanian head of state to Singapore in 10 years.
Speaking at a state banquet hosted in honour of President Mulino and his spouse, President Tharman said small states must work together to strengthen institutions that uphold international law amid trade disruptions and an unpredictable global landscape.
He added that Singapore and Panama share a deep interest in upholding freedom of navigation and international law, particularly the 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.
That is why Singapore has decided to accede to the protocol to the treaty concerning the permanent neutrality and operation of the Panama Canal, said President Tharman.
The treaty establishes a regime of permanent neutrality over the Panama Canal, which means – among other things – that the waterway will remain open for the peaceful transit of vessels of all nations in times of peace and war.
It was signed in 1977 by Panama and the US, which previously held control of the waterway.
The Panama Canal connects the Pacific and Atlantic oceans through Panama. The 82km-long waterway has in recent years been caught up in strategic competition between the US and China as both countries vie for influence over key ports.
Singapore’s decision signals its commitment to maritime safety and security, and to upholding freedom of navigation through the waterway, which is one of the world’s most important maritime arteries, said President Tharman.
Forty-one states, including France, Germany, Korea, Russia, Switzerland, Britain, the Philippines and Vietnam, have acceded to the protocol to the treaty, which was open for accession in 1979.
President Mulino was accompanied on his visit by a delegation comprising Panama Minister of Foreign Affairs Javier Eduardo Martinez-Acha Vasquez, Minister for Canal Affairs Jose Ramon Icaza and senior officials.
They were joined at the banquet by Singapore’s Minister for Foreign Affairs Vivian Balakrishnan, Minister for Law and Second Minister for Home Affairs Edwin Tong, Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport Murali Pillai and Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and National Development Alvin Tan.
President Tharman also noted that bilateral ties between Singapore and Panama have grown steadily since both countries established diplomatic relations 44 years ago in 1982, underpinned by their shared destinies and outlook as maritime nations.
In 2025, Panama was Singapore’s third-largest trading partner in goods in Latin America, with bilateral trade in goods, including imports from Panama like textiles, coffee and whisky, reaching $6.2 billion.
The two nations both sit at the strategic crossroads of global trade and serve as critical junctions on the “great maritime highway” between Asia and the Americas, noted President Tharman.
He said this shared history as maritime bridges makes Singapore and Panama natural partners with considerable room to deepen cooperation.
Singapore can also serve as a gateway for Panamanian companies to access South-east Asia, he noted.
Both countries have also agreed to begin negotiations on a bilateral mutual legal assistance treaty to strengthen information-sharing and legal cooperation, said President Tharman.
The agreement will provide an enhanced framework for both countries to make requests for and provide assistance with criminal investigations and proceedings, said the Ministry of Law on Oct 5.
President Tharman also announced that Singapore-based airport ground services provider SATS and Panama City’s Tocumen International Airport had signed a pact on Oct 5 to strengthen air cargo connectivity and support the development of Panama as a leading logistics gateway for the Americas.
Earlier in the day, President Mulino called on President Tharman and met Prime Minister Lawrence Wong at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA).
PM Wong and President Mulino discussed regional and international developments, as well as opportunities to strengthen cooperation in areas like trade and investment, logistics and connectivity, said MFA in a statement on Oct 5.
Both leaders also witnessed the signing of the deal between SATS and Tocumen International Airport at MFA.
In a social media post on Oct 5, PM Wong said: “There is much more we can do together, especially in logistics, given our roles as major air and maritime hubs.”
President Mulino, who became Panama’s leader in 2024, also visited the National Orchid Garden, where he had an orchid named in his honour.

articles.title: Vietnam’s GDP grows over 9 per cent in first nine months - Vietnam Investment Review - VIR
articles.summary: Vietnam’s GDP grows over 9 per cent in first nine months  Vietnam Investment Review - VIR
articles.full_text:
Twelve of the country's 34 provinces and cities recorded regional GDP growth of at least 10 per cent, led by Quang Ninh, Ha Tinh, and Haiphong.
The National Statistics Office (NSO) held a press conference on October 3 to announce the socioeconomic statistics for the third quarter and the first nine months. According to a report presented by NSO director general Nguyen Thi Huong, Vietnam's performance continued to deliver positive results across most sectors despite persistent global economic uncertainties.
| Vietnam's economic growth in the first nine months. Data source: NSO | 
Vietnam’s GDP is estimated to have expanded by 9.95 per cent on-year in the third quarter of 2026, accelerating from 8.15 per cent in the first quarter and 8.81 per cent in the second quarter. Agriculture, forestry, and fisheries grew by 4.21 per cent, while industry and construction expanded by 12.5 per cent, and services by 9.54 per cent.
For the first nine months, GDP growth reached an estimated 9.01 per cent. Agriculture, forestry, and fisheries grew by 4.02 per cent, contributing 5.35 per cent to the increase in the economy’s total gross value added. Industry and construction expanded by 11.21 per cent, contributing 49.62 per cent, while services grew by 8.69 per cent, accounting for 45.03 per cent.
Twelve of Vietnam’s 34 cities and provinces recorded regional GDP growth of at least 10 per cent. Quang Ninh led with 12.54 per cent, followed by Ha Tinh at 12.36 per cent, Haiphong at 12.08 per cent, Bac Ninh at 11.81 per cent, and Ninh Binh at 11.3 per cent.
Industrial growth remained robust, supported by expanding growth drivers, the operation of several large-scale projects, a recovery in export orders, and faster public investment disbursement, which generated spillover effects across manufacturing and construction.
Industrial gross value added rose by 11.02 per cent in the first nine months. Manufacturing and processing remained the main growth driver, expanding by 11.36 per cent and contributing 33.85 per cent to the increase in the economy’s total gross value added. Construction grew by 12.22 per cent, contributing 8.23 per cent.
The industrial production index is estimated to have increased by 14.8 per cent on-year in the third quarter. For the first nine months, the index rose by 12.3 per cent, the strongest nine-month increase since 2019. Manufacturing and processing grew by 12.9 per cent, electricity production and distribution by 10.6 per cent, and mining by 8 per cent.
The consumption index for the manufacturing and processing sector increased by 12.8 per cent over the nine-month period. Meanwhile, inventories in the sector as of September 30 were 11.9 per cent higher than a year earlier.
Within the services sector, transport and warehousing grew by 11.03 per cent on-year in the first nine months, followed by wholesale and retail trade at 9.85 per cent, financial, banking, and insurance activities at 9.45 per cent, and accommodation and food services at 8.83 per cent.
Total retail sales of goods and consumer service revenue at current prices were estimated at more than VND2 quadrillion ($80 billion) in the third quarter, up 14.5 per cent on-year. The figure reached almost VND6 quadrillion ($235 billion) in the first nine months, an increase of 13.4 per cent. Excluding price factors, growth stood at 7.8 per cent.
International arrivals reached an estimated 5.4 million in the third quarter, up 13.8 per cent on-year. The total for the first nine months was 17.7 million, an increase of 14.5 per cent.
Goods exports reached $167.85 billion in the third quarter, up 30.4 per cent on-year, while imports rose by 42.2 per cent to $170.33 billion.
For the first nine months, total goods trade reached $888.02 billion, up 30.4 per cent on-year. Exports increased by 24.5 per cent to $434.30 billion, while imports rose by 36.7 per cent to $453.72 billion.
Domestic enterprises accounted for $83.89 billion, or 19.3 per cent, of total exports, up 7.5 per cent on-year. Foreign-invested enterprises, including crude oil, generated $350.41 billion, up 29.4 per cent and accounting for the remaining 80.7 per cent.
Processed industrial products made up 90.4 per cent of total export value, while production materials accounted for 94.1 per cent of imports. The United States remained Vietnam’s largest export market, with shipments worth $140 billion, while China was the largest import source, with imports totalling $187.34 billion.
Vietnam recorded a goods trade surplus of $1.27 billion in September. However, the country posted a trade deficit of $19.42 billion for the first nine months, compared with a surplus of $16.87 billion in the same period last year. The services trade deficit reached $8.21 billion.
Total social investment at current prices was estimated at VND3.1 quadrillion ($121 billion) in the first nine months of 2026, up 15.1 per cent on-year, compared with growth of 11.6 per cent in the same period of 2025.
According to the NSO, the increase reflected the impact of macroeconomic management policies, efforts to accelerate public investment projects, and sustained confidence among domestic private businesses and foreign investors.
Investment by the state sector reached VND931 trillion ($36.5 billion), up 17.3 per cent. The non-state sector invested VND1.65 quadrillion ($64.5 billion), an increase of 14 per cent, while investment by foreign direct investment (FDI) enterprises totalled VND529.4 trillion ($20.5 billion), up 14.5 per cent.
Total registered foreign investment in Vietnam reached $50.36 billion as of September 30, up 76.4 per cent on-year. Disbursed FDI was estimated at $21.07 billion in the first nine months, an increase of 12.1 per cent and the highest nine-month figure since 2022.
The consumer price index (CPI) rose by an average of 4.8 per cent on-year in the third quarter. For the first nine months, average CPI inflation stood at 4.52 per cent, while core inflation reached 4.26 per cent.
NSO director general Nguyen Thi Huong said, "Nine-month GDP growth of 9.01 per cent was exceptionally high by historical standards and provided an important foundation for achieving the highest possible growth rate under the country's targets. However, achieving double-digit economic growth would remain a major challenge."
The NSO called for continued efforts to prioritise growth while maintaining macroeconomic stability, ensuring major economic balances, controlling inflation and prices, and stabilising markets.

articles.title: Xuan Thien Group proposes port, steel and energy complex in central Vietnam - Theinvestor
articles.summary: Xuan Thien Group proposes port, steel and energy complex in central Vietnam  Theinvestor
articles.full_text:
Vietnamese multi-sector group Xuan Thien has proposed studying an industrial, urban, tourism, seaport services and energy complex in the Chan May-Lang Co Economic Zone in Hue city.
The steering committee overseeing key projects in Hue for the 2025-2030 term recently met with Xuan Thien Group to discuss its investment proposal in Chan May-Lang Co.
The proposed components include Chan May Port, a liquid and gas storage facility, a concrete components plant, an urban-services area and housing for workers and employees, and a high-tech steel complex combined with a cogeneration power plant.
The projects are designed to link seaports, logistics, raw material supply, industrial production, energy, urban development and services.
Xuan Thien estimates that the complex would create direct and indirect jobs for local workers while supporting the development of supporting industries, logistics and related services.
The scale, technology and investment plans are still being studied, reviewed and refined before being submitted to relevant authorities for consideration.
At the meeting, participants focused on planning, land, infrastructure, water supply and environmental protection requirements. Technology selection was required to be aligned with efficient resource use, energy conservation, greater circularity, and water recycling.
Prioritizing individual projects
Hue People's Committee Chairman Le Tri Thanh asked Xuan Thien to develop the seaport as part of a broader expansion of industrial space, ensuring sufficient cargo-handling capacity and seamless connections with related projects.
For the Chan May port system, the city called for an appropriate allocation of berths by function, including areas for container, bulk and liquid cargo, as well as cruise ships.
The plans should assess technical conditions, operating capacity, infrastructure connectivity and impacts on existing residential areas.
Residential planning should also take into account living conditions and long-term livelihoods. If resettlement is required, plans should integrate housing, schools, infrastructure and community facilities.
For households engaged in fishing, the city asked that housing arrangements be studied in conjunction with boat anchorage areas to help maintain their livelihoods. Access to the sea, public beaches and service activities should also be considered in the planning process.
The city asked relevant agencies to work with Xuan Thien to review planning and land-use arrangements, complete procedures for priority components and study transport links between the project area and the port.
The water supply plan must meet production and residential needs, have the capacity to supplement supplies as demand rises and be linked to water-resource protection.
Hue Party Committee Secretary Nguyen Dinh Trung asked Xuan Thien to review the entire proposal, determine priorities and establish an implementation roadmap, with foundational components planned in line with the group's ability to mobilize capital and actual implementation conditions.
The Hue People's Committee was tasked with directing relevant departments, agencies and local authorities to work with the group to review planning, guide the completion of dossiers and procedures, study technical and social infrastructure development, and prepare the necessary workforce.
Worker housing, social housing and accommodation for experts should be integrated with education, healthcare, cultural facilities and essential amenities, the city said.
Trung also called for consideration of establishing a working group to monitor and accelerate investment preparations, with clear responsibilities for the lead agency, coordinating units, and deadlines for each task.
The implementation process must balance the interests of the state, businesses and local residents while prioritizing environmental protection, landscape preservation, and the natural values of the Chan May-Lang Co area.
Established in 2000, the Ninh Binh province-headquartered Xuan Thien Group operates primarily in the fields of energy, materials, and agriculture.
